question: Is activated PI3K-delta syndrome inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, which means one copy of the altered gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the disorder.
greedy_answer:
Activated PI3K-delta syndrome is a rare genetic disorder. It is caused by mutations in the PIK3CD gene, which encodes the p110δ subunit of the PI3Kδ enzyme. This enzyme plays a crucial role in the immune system, particularly in the function of T cells and B cells.

The PIK3CD gene is located on the X chromosome. As a result, activated PI3K-delta syndrome is typically inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. This means that a single copy of the mutated gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition.

In females, who have two X chromosomes, the condition can be inherited from either parent. If a female inherits one mutated copy of the PIK3CD gene, she has a 50% chance of passing it to each of her sons and daughters. Sons who inherit the mutated gene will be affected, while daughters who inherit the mutated gene will be carriers, like their mother.

In males, who have only one X chromosome, a single copy of the mutated gene is enough to cause the condition. If a male inherits the mutated PIK3CD gene, he will be affected.
